title: Graph snapshot load rebuilds each restored relation basis by scanning every item and blocker
outcome: Graph snapshot load rebuilds each restored relation basis by scanning every item and blocker
acceptance: restored_relation_basis's cost in graph snapshot load is linear in the snapshot's items and blockers across both call paths (the Native-record check and the per-newest-item check), proven by a test-only visit counter on equal-size fixtures that differ in record count, with canonical order and bytes unchanged
Every refusal and its order in the load path stay as today, covered by the existing load tests

completion.summary: Graph snapshot load now indexes the items and groups the blockers once (RelationBases, built in prepare_load after the relation pass), builds each item's relation basis on first demand at the same two call sites as before (native record materialization; the lifecycle check) and reuses it, and finds each item's newest record in one pass over the records; every refusal keeps its text and place, a native record is minted from the same elements in the same order, and carried records keep their recorded relations byte for byte. Proven by tests/relation_bases.rs: two test-only counters show basis work equal to items + blockers + items whether each item has one or three generations (real revisions between save→load→save rounds), and newest visits equal to the record count; the loader's bases equal a reference computed without it and carried record ids and canonical bytes survive a further load and save; refusal places pinned (native duplicate, carried-only duplicate at the lifecycle check, dangling record first, item without records) with no partial state.
